what: A list of tables: one sheet each
title: Writing Excel workbooks with write_xlsx()
text: Give write_xlsx() named list every table gets sheet, named list item. Calling generate_frequency() several variables returns list, named variable labels, can write directly: Sheet names follow Excel’s rules: / (written ” “) 31 characters. longer name error, notice label cut middle word. Set trim_sheet_names = TRUE cut long names instead; names clash numbered (2), (3). Unnamed list items become Table 1, Table 2, . pass title list, sheet gets "<title>: <sheet name>" unless table already title :
code: tables <- list(   Sex = generate_frequency(person_record, sex),   Marital = generate_frequency(person_record, marital_status),   Employment = generate_crosstab(person_record, employed, sex) )  write_xlsx(tables, "tables.xlsx") openxlsx::getSheetNames("tables.xlsx") #> [1] "Sex"        "Marital"    "Employment" several <- generate_frequency(person_record, sex, employed, seeing) names(several) #> [1] "Sex"                             "Employment status"               #> [3] "Seeing, even if wearing glasses" long_names <- generate_frequency(person_record, hearing, walking) names(long_names) #> [1] "Hearing, even if using hearing aid"                             #> [2] "Walking or climbing steps, even if with cane or artificial leg"  write_xlsx(long_names, "long-names.xlsx", trim_sheet_names = TRUE) openxlsx::getSheetNames("long-names.xlsx") #> [1] "Hearing, even if using hearing"  "Walking or climbing steps, even" write_xlsx(tables, "tables-titled.xlsx", title = "Household survey", source_note = "Source: person_record")

text: Keys part.property. parts table, title, subtitle, header, spanner (upper rows multi-level header), body, col_first, col_last, row_group, sub_group, source_note, footnotes, border_header, border_outer, border_bottom label. Style properties follow openxlsx::createStyle(): fontName, fontSize, fontColour, numFmt, border, borderColour, borderStyle, bgFill, fgFill, halign, valign, textDecoration, wrapText indent. fgFill fill colour cell; bgFill background Excel fill pattern shows behind one (HTML Word use fgFill unset). Colours hexadecimal codes (e.g. "#FF0000") colour names. border "top", "bottom", "left" "right"; borderStyle uses Excel names ("thin", "medium", "thick", "dashed", "dotted", "double", "hair", "mediumDashed", "dashDot", ...) every output format; HTML, PDF Word translate nearest line. keys style every output format. Settings mean something spreadsheet (height, width, table.offsetRow, table.offsetCol, table.gridLines, table.tabColour, table.locked, table.hidden, table.widthOffset, indent, wrapText) ignored HTML, PDF Word. Layout properties: height: row height points (border_bottom.height last header row multi-level header). width: column width (table.width columns, col_first.width category column, row_group.width grouping columns , col_last.width last). unset (~) col_first.width row_group.width fits column's content. table.offsetRow, table.offsetCol: rows columns left empty table. table.gridLines, table.tabColour, table.hidden: worksheet grid lines, tab colour visibility. table.decimalPrecision: decimal places numeric columns fractional values; numbers shown whole numbers thousands separators. category grouping columns formatted. table.decimalCols: names columns show decimals (even values whole); numeric columns shown whole numbers. Excel, HTML, PDF Word. table.lastRowBold: bold last row. border_outer.border: outer sides table get border, "top", "bottom", "left" "right". body.bandFill: fill colour every body row (banded rows); default. table.widthOffset: width offset columns. label.titleTableList, label.backHyperlink: name table-list sheet text link back . facade file (facade list passed writer), key set ~ (NULL) turns setting instead falling back default. add_facade() NULL value ignored, turn setting one table.
